title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship — agents that review, fix, and approve GitHub pull requests
subtitle: The new suite pairs the generally available Code Review with two beta agents: PR Steward, which pushes fixes, and Claude Approvals, which votes approve-or-block against a repo policy file.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic launched Claude Ship on November 23 — a three-part suite of pull-request agents for Claude Team and Enterprise customers on GitHub. Code Review ships generally available. PR Steward and Claude Approvals enter beta. PR Steward responds to failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback by pushing commits with fixes; by design it cannot approve or merge. Claude Approvals reads a policy file in the repository and votes approve-or-block when the organization configures it as a required GitHub check.

The split matters. PR Steward handles the mechanical work a human reviewer would otherwise bounce back, and Claude Approvals makes the accept-or-reject call — but only against a policy the team wrote, with any classifiers inside that policy billed on the tokens they use. There is no base charge for Claude Approvals itself. Anthropic recommends starting in observe-only mode before gating merges through branch protection, and administrators can set spend limits on Code Review and PR Steward.

Claude Ship lands two days after Anthropic's Nasdaq debut and in the same week as Enterprise Frontier Safeguards. It is Anthropic's clearest commitment yet to autonomous code review — not just suggestions in a comment thread, but a signed approver on the pull request. Eligible Claude Enterprise organizations can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits through January 15, 2027.

A note for learners: automated code review is the easy part — automated approval is where policy design starts to matter. A policy file that encodes 'what a human reviewer would catch' is a specification problem, and you should write it the way you'd write a contract with an outsourced team. If you work in a codebase that adopts tools like Claude Approvals, read that file before you read the review bot's output: it tells you what the bot is allowed to care about.
